request: Show the monarch butterfly migration on a map, it's for a nature short.
intent: Nature fans want to see the route and the surprise behind it.
goal: The viewer can trace the route and knows no butterfly has made the trip before.
promise: A journey across a continent by an insect.
arc: A map, the route drawing south from Canada to Mexico, the whole path held, then generations along it.

events.text: Every autumn, monarch butterflies leave southern Canada and fly south.
events.job: Start the journey on the map.
events.look: the start in southern Canada on the map

events.text: Down through the United States, up to four thousand kilometers, to the same mountain forests in central Mexico.
events.knows: Up to 4000 km to central Mexico.
events.look: the route drawing south across the map

holds.does: the route ends at the forest; the whole path stays in view

demo.what: the route drawn across the map

phases.why: the route follows the words down the continent

events.text: None of them has ever been there. Their great-grandparents made the last trip.
events.knows: No butterfly has made the trip before; earlier generations did.

reveal.what: that none of them has been there

quiz.q: Where does the migration start and end?
quiz.a: Southern Canada to the mountain forests of central Mexico.

quiz.q: What is surprising about the butterflies that make the trip?
quiz.a: None of them has been there before; their great-grandparents made the last trip.

quiz.q: Which way did the route move on the map?
quiz.a: South, down from Canada through the United States to Mexico.

quiz.q: On the map, is the start above or below the end?
At the end of the drawing, what stayed in view?
Where along the picture were the generations placed?
